items.text: The FBI is investigating an apparent hack of the National Crime Information Center (NCIC). Police at every level use the database for warrants, missing persons, criminal histories, stolen property and background checks. CNN reported it first, and the AP and NBC confirmed it through people familiar with the matter. The FBI declined to comment and the scope is not yet clear. In a Fox News interview on Saturday Trump said the administration had just heard about it and that it is 'not good', though he also suggested it could be given 'a positive spin'. If confirmed, this is the FBI's second major breach this year, after the September ShinyHunters claim. It also follows a run of federal outages (the FAA ground stop and NSANet) that officials blamed on routine upgrades.
items.notes: Based on anonymous sources (CNN, NBC, AP). The FBI has not confirmed and Director Patel has not commented. Al Jazeera dates the first reports to Friday Nov 20 and Trump's comment to Saturday Nov 21. Some outlets suggested a link to a Russia probe ('Russia hoax' remark), but the AP says there is no sign of a link to the earlier outages.

items.text: The Agriculture Department is dealing with a security incident that its cyber operations centre found last week. According to internal emails seen by Nextgov/FCW, IT staff reset every database password across all environments, which took many applications offline for several days. Affected systems include payment tools for farmers (crop insurance and loss-coverage programmes), client portals for loan and aid status, and some staff VPN access. On Nov 21 NBC described it as an apparent cyberattack, and farm-trade outlets cite claims that Russian-speaking hackers were involved. Nextgov says it is unclear who was behind the intrusion or whether data was taken.
items.notes: Nextgov first reported this on Nov 19 and NBC's 'cyberattack' report came on Nov 21 (via Al Jazeera). The Russian-speaking-hacker attribution is unverified (AgWeb 'allegedly'). USDA and CISA have not commented on the record.

items.text: Trump told Fox News that he hopes Iran tries to run the US blockade of its ports with a reported 14-tanker convoy from Kharg Island, and that the ships would sink 'like the rest of the navy'. On Sunday the UK Maritime Trade Operations centre reported an incident in the Gulf of Oman involving a tanker and military forces. It did not name the vessel or link it to the convoy. Maritime-sanctions expert Charlie Brown (UANI) called the convoy plan likely propaganda, saying satellite images show no significant loading at Kharg, while ISW warned that an attempt could come within days. CENTCOM said on Nov 18 that ships taking Iranian cargo through ship-to-ship transfers may also be seized.
items.notes: The convoy is reported only by Iranian outlet Hamshahri and Euronews and has not been confirmed. The UKMTO incident is not linked to it. Fox leans right; Al Jazeera is a counterweight on the blockade's reach. A Newsmax headline (Nov 22) says Trump claimed Iran's weekly missile and drone attacks hit a high, but the article could not be read.

items.text: US District Judge Mary McElroy in Providence ruled that HUD unlawfully tried to remake the Continuum of Care homelessness programme, which has more than $4bn in FY2026 funding. HUD planned to set aside $1.3bn for transitional housing and service-only grants, moving away from the housing-first model. She found HUD exceeded its authority under the McKinney-Vento Act by adding criteria that bypass reviews of existing projects' performance. She also struck down a ban on grantee activities aimed at drug users, such as needle exchanges, and a rule letting HUD disqualify applicants that do not promote 'self-sufficiency'. HUD must let applicants amend and resubmit through Dec 1 and award funds by Dec 31. The plaintiffs are 22 mostly Democratic-led states, DC and advocacy groups.
items.notes: Late catch from Nov 20, not logged before. This is a renewed challenge, on different grounds, after an appeals court lifted McElroy's earlier injunction. HUD did not comment and an appeal is likely. The Epoch Times (right-leaning) also covers it as 'key parts' blocked.

items.text: US District Judge Trina Thompson in San Francisco ruled that Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins violated the First Amendment's establishment clause with religious messages sent from her official email to USDA's roughly 100,000 employees. She pointed to Rollins's authority over staff and to wording that presented Christianity as a shared faith. Rollins must stop proselytizing staff, stop when asked and not use her position to pressure subordinates. She may still talk about her faith and politely invite colleagues to religious events. Six employees and the National Federation of Federal Employees brought the suit in May, and USDA says it is considering an appeal.
items.notes: Late catch, not logged before. The roundup dates it Nov 20, while La Nación (wire) says Thursday Nov 19.

items.text: US District Judge William Young in Massachusetts reportedly ruled unconstitutional the administration's transgender-related conditions on Ryan White HIV/AIDS programme grants. The conditions required grantees to comply with administration orders on gender identity in order to receive funding. Details of the remedy were not available in the source found.
items.notes: Single, less-established roundup. Needs confirmation from a wire or court docket before it gets prominent use. Late catch (Nov 19).

items.text: The Federal Communications Commission voted on Thursday to bar China Mobile, China Telecom, China Unicom and other covered IP-enabled providers from direct access to US telephone numbers. It cited national security and the need to curb scam robocalls. The three carriers were already barred from providing international telecom services to the US. Weekend headlines say Beijing vowed to defend its companies' interests.
items.notes: The vote date is inferred: SCMP says 'Thursday' and its image path is dated Nov 20. The Chinese reaction comes only from a headline in a Nov 22 digest and was not read in full. The FCC order text was not checked.
